title: AI Visual Interviewer Standardized Technical Evaluation Rubric
description: Standardized evaluation framework for objective, evidence-based technical assessment. Evaluates candidate responses across four weighted competency dimensions.

technical_depth.name: Technical Depth & Domain Accuracy
technical_depth.description: Evaluates architectural correctness, internal mechanisms, memory models, protocols, algorithms, and domain-specific knowledge.

1.label: Poor / Fundamentally Incorrect
1.criteria: Provides incorrect facts, displays major technical misconceptions, or fails to understand core architectural concepts.

2.label: Weak / Significant Gaps
2.criteria: Demonstrates superficial knowledge with critical omissions, confuses basic primitives, or relies on incorrect technical assumptions.

3.label: Average / Adequate
3.criteria: Correctly explains standard mechanics and definitions, but lacks depth regarding edge cases, internal implementation, or trade-offs.

4.label: Strong / Mostly Complete
4.criteria: Comprehensive understanding of technical concepts, accurate terminology, clear articulation of underlying mechanisms and operational trade-offs.

5.label: Excellent / Deep & Authoritative
5.criteria: Mastery of system internals, low-level execution details, failure modes, concurrency, memory models, and advanced optimization nuances.

problem_solving.name: Problem Solving & Analytical Logic
problem_solving.description: Evaluates structured reasoning, root cause analysis, methodical trade-off evaluation, and logical problem decomposition.

1.label: Poor / Illogical Approach
1.criteria: Lacks structure, proposes contradictory or dangerous solutions, and exhibits no clear reasoning process.

2.label: Weak / Disorganized Reasoning
2.criteria: Jumps to hasty conclusions without analyzing constraints, overlooks obvious failure modes, and struggles to break down complexity.

3.label: Average / Standard Methodical Approach
3.criteria: Follows a reasonable step-by-step approach to arrive at a viable solution, but does not thoroughly evaluate alternative trade-offs.

4.label: Strong / Systematic & Rigorous
4.criteria: Methodically decomposes problems, identifies edge cases, evaluates trade-offs between speed/memory/complexity, and justifies design choices.

5.label: Excellent / Multi-Dimensional Synthesis
5.criteria: Exceptional first-principles reasoning, anticipates second-order failure modes, proactively optimizes bottlenecks, and validates edge boundaries.

practical_experience.name: Practical Experience & Production Readiness
practical_experience.description: Evaluates real-world production experience, debugging instincts, operational monitoring, resiliency, schema migrations, and tool mastery.

1.label: Poor / No Practical Understanding
1.criteria: Purely theoretical or incorrect understanding with no sense of real-world constraints or production safety.

2.label: Weak / Limited Practical Exposure
2.criteria: Limited to toy/tutorial examples; ignores production realities such as connection pooling, indexing costs, rate limits, or logging.

3.label: Average / Competent Practical Knowledge
3.criteria: Familiar with standard production patterns, tooling, and basic deployment workflows, but lacks experience with high-scale challenges.

4.label: Strong / Proven Production Instincts
4.criteria: Cites realistic production patterns, observability, disaster recovery, zero-downtime migrations, caching layers, and troubleshooting steps.

5.label: Excellent / Battle-Tested Engineering
5.criteria: Deep production war stories, advanced telemetry/tracing, capacity planning, distributed transactions, zero-trust security, and resilience engineering.

communication_clarity.name: Communication Clarity & Structure
communication_clarity.description: Evaluates clarity, concise delivery, structured explanations (top-down / pyramid principle), and professional technical communication.

1.label: Poor / Incoherent
1.criteria: Rambling, highly disjointed, unintelligible, or completely unresponsive to the specific question asked.

2.label: Weak / Vague & Unfocused
2.criteria: Overly verbose or vague, requires significant effort to parse core points, uses ambiguous language, and strays off topic.

3.label: Average / Clear & Understandable
3.criteria: Adequately communicates ideas and answers the prompt, though structure could be tightened and technical precision improved.

4.label: Strong / Well-Structured & Concise
4.criteria: Delivers clear, structured explanations with high signal-to-noise ratio, appropriate technical terminology, and logical flow.

5.label: Excellent / Masterful Technical Articulation
5.criteria: Crisp, executive-level technical communication, perfect pacing, clear hierarchical breakdown, and exemplary precision.

evidence_rules.evidence_first_principle: Every numerical score awarded when status is ANSWERED must be justified by verbatim quotes extracted directly from the candidate transcript.
evidence_rules.verbatim_requirement: Quotes in direct_quotes must match character-for-character (case-insensitive with whitespace normalization) with segments from candidate_transcript.
evidence_rules.anti_hallucination_rule: The evaluator must NEVER invent, extrapolate, or paraphrase candidate words into direct_quotes.

no_answer_handling.description: When a candidate remains silent, submits an empty recording, explicitly states I do not know, or provides no substantive attempt at answering.
no_answer_handling.scoring_rule: Do NOT assign a competency score of 1.0. Instead, set all score fields (technical_depth, problem_solving, practical_experience, communication_clarity, overall_score) to null. This prevents confounding absence of response with incompetent response.
no_answer_handling.direct_quotes_rule: Must be an empty array [] since no candidate answer evidence exists.
gaps_identified: Candidate did not provide a substantive response to the question.
no_answer_handling.scoring_rationale: Candidate provided no answer (silence, pass, or empty submission).
